framework: Income-tax Act, 2025 (rates carried forward from Finance (No.2) Act 2024; Finance Act 2026)
notes: Finance Act 2026 made no change to the STCG (20%), LTCG (12.5%) or ₹1,25,000 exemption rates; its capital gains change is the tax treatment of share buy-backs. For land or buildings acquired before 23 July 2024, resident individuals/HUFs pay the lower of 12.5% without indexation or 20% with indexation. Cost Inflation Index per CBDT (2026-27: 384). Cess is 4%.
assumptions: Reflects statutory capital gains rates for FY 2026-27 (TY 2026-27); Finance Act 2026 did not change them.
Listed equity shares and equity-oriented mutual funds: Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) taxed at 20%; Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) taxed at 12.5% on gains exceeding the ₹1,25,000 annual exemption.

Immovable property held for more than 24 months qualifies as LTCG and is taxed at 12.5% without indexation. If acquired before 23 July 2024, a resident individual/HUF pays the lower of 12.5% without indexation and 20% with indexation (CBDT Cost Inflation Index).
A mandatory 4% Health and Education Cess is added to computed tax.
limitations: Does not calculate statutory rollover exemptions under Section 54, Section 54EC, or Section 54F for reinvestment into property or specified bonds.
Does not compute Fair Market Value (FMV) grandfathering adjustments for equity assets acquired prior to 1 February 2018.
Does not compute set-off of capital losses against capital gains or inter-year loss carry-forward balances under Section 70 and 71.
Estimated tax computation; consult Schedule CG of official ITR-2 form for definitive filing.
For property acquired before 1 April 2001, indexation uses CII 100 and the cost should be the fair market value as on 1 April 2001.
disclaimer: This calculator uses the rules/data published by Income Tax Department (CBDT) for FY 2026-27 (TY 2026-27). Estimated result based on the inputs and assumptions provided. Educational tool only; not legal or filing advice. Check official guidance for your specific situation.

values.debtFund50AANote: Section 50AA (Finance Act 2023): units of specified (debt) mutual funds acquired on or after 1 April 2023 are always short-term, whatever the holding period. The 24-month debt-fund threshold above applies only to units acquired before that date.
